title: Soy-Ginger Glazed Chicken Leg Quarters
equipment: Wire rack that fits the sheet pan

items: 4 chicken leg quarters (about 3 lb total), fully thawed
¼ cup packed dark brown sugar
4 green onions, whites and greens sliced separately

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, mirin, molasses, oil, ginger, garlic, dry mustard, red pepper flakes and green onion whites until the sugar dissolves. Pour ⅓ cup into a small saucepan, cover and refrigerate it for the glaze. Save the green onion greens for the end.
Put the chicken in a gallon zip-top bag with the rest of the marinade. Seal and refrigerate 4–12 hr, turning once. Past 12 hr the soy makes the meat taste cured.

Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the upper middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set a wire rack on it. Lift the chicken from the marinade, pat the skin dry, and set it skin side up on the rack. Throw out the used marinade.
Roast 40–45 min, until the thickest thigh reads 175°F and the skin is deep brown.

While it roasts, stir the cornstarch into the cold water. Bring the reserved marinade to a simmer over medium heat, stir in the cornstarch mixture, and simmer 1–2 min, stirring, until glossy and thick.
Switch the oven to broil. Brush the glaze over the chicken and broil 2–4 min, until lacquered and charred at the edges. Watch closely, since the sugar burns fast.
Top with the green onion greens and sesame seeds.
tips: The rack keeps the chicken out of the sugary drippings, which scorch on a bare pan.
To grill it instead, cook over indirect heat at about 375°F for 40–45 min, then brush with glaze and cook over direct heat 1–2 min per side.
Serve with the Hawaiian Pineapple Rice, or jasmine rice and steamed broccoli.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat in a 375°F oven 15–20 min, until it reaches 165°F.
